newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says $50 mln China investment cap flexible.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says $50 mln China investment cap flexible.

text.p: Taiwan said on Wednesday that exceptions to its newly imposed US$50 million ceiling on single investment projects in rival China were possible in cases where larger projects were beneficial.

"If a project exceeds US$50 million, it needs special policy consideration to ensure that it benefits sound interaction across the strait and is positive to local (Taiwan) economic development," the economic ministry said in a statement.

Economic minister Wang Chih-kang earlier announced new restrictions on investments in the Chinese mainland, including a US$50 million project cap, but vowed to drop the rules if Beijing renounced the right to retake the island by force.
Under the new rules, effective July 1, Taiwan firms are explicitly forbidden to invest in mainland infrastructure projects such as railways, harbours, airports, water works, roads and power plants.

Since a political thaw began in the late 1980s, some 30,000 Taiwan firms have poured over US$30 billion into the mainland -- routing their investments through third countries. As a result, Taiwan has become one of China's top overseas investors and China one of Taiwan's most important markets.
Communist China regards Nationalist-ruled Taiwan as a rebel-held province that must be brought under mainland sovereignty, preferably through peaceful means but by force of arms if necessary.
